thread:
priya: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a split control plane: Admin-CP (hosted by Redwood) + Data-CP (lightweight control plane that runs inside the customer's VPC). Goal: keep policy, billing, and user mgmt in Admin-CP; push session routing, auth tokens, and local KV cache pointers into Data-CP to cut egress and meet some compliance asks. open for tradeoffs and a proposed bootstrap flow.

ashwin: high level i'm +1, but we need to be explicit about what lives where. we should avoid making Data-CP responsible for model binaries or heavy state. Data-CP should be session-oriented only (routing, auth, prefix cache pointers).

leo: routing questions: how do we actually wire traffic to our DP (inference pods)? options: 1) short-lived peering/TGW attachment from our DP into customer VPC (expensive + route churn), 2) customer-side Data-CP opens outbound tunnel to our relay (we already have patterns), 3) PrivateLink endpoints per region + ALB/NLB. each has cost/ops/security tradeoffs.

maya: security note: if Data-CP runs in customer VPC we cannot assume Redwood KMS access. we need a clear KMS/HSM plan: either customer-managed KMS (we get wrapped keys) or short-lived certificates provisioned by Admin-CP via an enrollment flow. also data plane credentials must be zero-knowledge in our side for some customers.

priya: exactly. thinking of a 3-step bootstrap flow: 1) customer installs Data-CP (helm/operator) -> generates local keypair + CSR 2) Data-CP calls Admin-CP enroll API over outbound TLS (no inbound required) with CSR and tenancy proof 3) Admin-CP issues short-lived certs & scope tokens; Data-CP then establishes mTLS websocket with Redwood relays for session routing. this avoids peering.

ashwin: quick sketch of enroll call (pseudo):

```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.example/v1/enroll \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"cust-123","csr":"-----BEGIN CERT..."}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bootstrap-token>'
```

ashwin: Admin-CP validates bootstrap-token (from onboarding flow), returns cert + allowed routes (json list of model route prefixes and relay endpoints). Data-CP connects outbound to the assigned relays.

leo: operationally nice because outbound-only avoids opening customer firewalls. concerns: scaling of relays and routing table explosion if many customers use path-based routing. we could multiplex tenants on shared relays with SNI and mTLS.

maya: also add: attestation step for operator-managed clusters: use instance identity / cloud provider attestation in the enroll flow so we reduce risk of fake Data-CP claiming tenant_id.

sam: latency/cost tradeoff: if Data-CP only handles control and routing pointers, we still egress tokens and small KV entries. That reduces egress a lot vs peering. but for high-throughput customers who want pure private inference (models in their VPC), this doesn't solve it. we should treat this as a 'hybrid control' pattern, not fully private inference.

priya: Agreed. We should make two explicit profiles in the RFC: "Hybrid Control" (this new pattern) and "Local Inference" (customer runs models locally—different checklist). This thread is only about Hybrid Control.

leo: failure modes: if Admin-CP is unreachable, Data-CP must still honor cached policies and route to failover relays. propose: Admin-CP issues signed policy blobs with expiry. Data-CP enforces locally until expiry; it also keeps last-known relay list.

maya: compliance: log ingestion problem — customers want logs to their SIEM. Data-CP should support a local-forwarder interface (syslog/HTTP) so logs never leave customer network unless allowed. good design point.

ashwin: rollout and backward compatibility: Admin-CP must be able to talk to both legacy single-CP dataplanes and the new split Data-CP. consider a versioned enroll API and protocol version attached to certs.

priya: compatibility + canary plan: 1) implement Data-CP v1 as opt-in for beta customers; 2) make Admin-CP able to issue both v1 and v0 tokens; 3) provide fallbacks: if Data-CP can't connect to relays, we allow an "egress-relay-proxy" that the customer can opt into which opens an outbound tunnel to our relay for a transitional period.

leo: cost ops: PrivateLink eliminates NAT/route table sprawl but is $$$ per endpoint. outbound tunnel + multiplexed relays likely the lowest infra cost and easiest for customers to accept. we should prototype both to gather numbers.

maya: one more security detail: certificate revocation. short-lived certs help but we need to support immediate revocation (e.g., compromised key). suggest a revocation list service and a quick push notification channel from Admin-CP to relays.

sam: telemetry: Data-CP should emit per-tenant token usage, session counts, and last-seen relays. expose these in Console. also need alerting when Data-CP clock skew > N seconds (affects cert expiry).

priya: ops checklist I'm drafting: install/operator docs, enroll API spec, attestation options (oidc, aws-mlc), cert lifetime defaults (15m/1h/24h?), fallback policy semantics, log-forwarding interface, RBAC surface, and canary rollout playbook. comments?

ashwin: please add a note about KV cache invalidation semantics. if Admin-CP revokes a route, Data-CP must accept signed tombstones to avoid serving stale routing entries.

leo: i'll prototype an outbound ws-based relay handshake this week and report perf numbers (multiplexing 100 tenants per connection). will post results here.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary pipeline triggered for branch "data-cp/bootstrap-proto" — staging cluster x3. :rocket:

priya: awesome. thanks all — i'll update the RFC with the bootstrap flow and the canary checklist. we should aim for a short beta next quarter.
